newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Postal Service to continue Sunday deliveries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Postal Service to continue Sunday deliveries.

text.p: The Postal Service said Friday it would continue Sunday deliveries in select areas as it handles an increased volume of mail as a result of the Teamsters strike against United Parcel Service.

Nicholas Barranca, an official with the Postal Service, also told NBC's "Today" show that the service had hired about 4,100 employees to handle the crush and that most mail was being delivered on time.

When asked if the Sunday deliveries would continue from last weekend, Barranca said: "Yes, they will, they'll be delivered where needed. That's a local call and local managers are assessing their personal volumes."
He said the Postal Service had taken a number of other measures to cope with the increased demand.
"We've increased window time so that customers can bring parcels into the Postal Service," Barranca said.

"We've added additional transportation, and last weekend we also delivered, in addition to our express mail on Sunday, we delivered our priority two- and three-day product and also our ground parcel service product also."

He also told NBC the Postal Service had primarily hired additional mail handlers after an agreement was reached with the union representing the handlers before the Teamsters strike, now in its 12th day.
